summary.one_liner: Threema Web is a browser-based desktop client for the Threema end-to-end encrypted messenger, connecting to the mobile app via WebRTC or encrypted WebSockets.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a web client so Threema mobile users can use Threema on a desktop browser. The desktop and phone connect through WebRTC (Android) or encrypted WebSockets (iOS). Signaling and data are end-to-end encrypted with SaltyRTC. The README describes the protocol between the Threema app and Threema Web as documented separately. The project is written in TypeScript with AngularJS 1 and built with npm, and it includes unit and UI test suites plus a lint task. Configuration is done through src/config.ts and userconfig files, and the Docker image lets userconfig variables be overridden with environment variables. Self-hosting instructions are in docs/self_hosting.md. The README also notes a translation process via TRANSLATING.md.
use_cases: use Threema messenger on a desktop browser
self-host a web client for Threema
end-to-end encrypted chat from a computer
run a private Threema web frontend in Docker
contribute translations for a messaging client
how_to_run: For production self-hosting, follow docs/self_hosting.md (dev server is not for production)
notable: Connects to the phone app over WebRTC on Android and encrypted WebSockets on iOS
Signaling and data end-to-end encrypted with SaltyRTC
Docker image allows runtime userconfig overrides via environment variables
Publishes a CycloneDX VEX file documenting dependency vulnerability assessments
caveats: Currently in maintenance mode: only regular maintenance and critical bug fixes, no major new features
Dev server setup must not be used in production
